3.happening: We choose inf = {inf} as a stand-in for 'not solvable / not yet solved'.
3.why: Any real coin count is smaller, so inf is safe to compare against.
3.invariant: inf is larger than any achievable coin count.

4.happening: We build the memo table with one slot per amount, all set to inf.
4.why: Every sub-amount's answer will be cached here exactly once.
4.invariant: A cell holding inf means that amount is still unsolved.

5.happening: We seed the base case: memo[0] = 0.
5.why: It takes zero coins to make the amount zero.

6.happening: We start solving the full target amount {amount}.
6.why: The recursion breaks it into smaller sub-amounts.
6.invariant: The answer to amount is built from answers to smaller amounts.

7.happening: best is still the sentinel, so amount {amount} cannot be formed.
7.why: No sequence of coins ever reached it.
7.invariant: An unreachable amount stays at inf.

7.happening: best dropped below inf, so a real coin count was found.
7.why: At least one coin combination reached the amount.
7.invariant: A solvable amount holds a finite coin count.

8.happening: We convert the sentinel to -1 to report impossibility.
8.why: The problem asks for -1 when the amount cannot be made.
8.invariant: best now holds the reportable answer.

9.why: It is the minimum coins for the amount, or -1.
9.invariant: The returned value is the final answer.

12.happening: This sub-amount is 0 — the base case.
12.why: Nothing more is needed to make zero.

12.happening: Sub-amount {amt} is positive, so it must be solved.
12.why: Positive amounts need at least one coin.
12.invariant: We only recurse on non-negative amounts.

13.happening: We return 0 for the empty amount.
13.invariant: The base case never uses a coin.

14.why: Recomputing it would waste work — this is the whole point of memoization.
14.invariant: Each sub-amount is computed at most once.

14.happening: memo[{amt}] is still inf, so this amount is unsolved.
14.invariant: An unsolved cell is computed exactly once, then cached.

15.happening: We reuse the cached answer memo[{amt}] = {memo[amt]}.
15.why: The sub-amount was solved earlier in the recursion.
15.invariant: The memo makes repeated sub-amounts free.

16.happening: We set this amount's best to inf (unknown so far).
16.why: Each candidate coin will try to lower it.
16.invariant: best only ever decreases from inf.

17.happening: We try coin {c} as the last coin used.
17.why: The best answer is the smallest over all coin choices.

18.happening: Coin {c} fits in the remaining amount {amt}.
18.why: Only usable coins can lead to a valid solution.
18.invariant: We never take a coin larger than the amount.

18.happening: Coin {c} is larger than {amt}, so it is skipped.
18.why: It cannot be part of solving this amount.

19.why: Solving the remainder tells us how many coins that part needs.
19.invariant: The remainder is strictly smaller, so recursion terminates.

20.happening: Adding this coin costs one more than the remainder: cand = {sub} + 1.
20.why: Using coin {c} contributes exactly one coin.
20.invariant: cand counts the coin just used plus the remainder's coins.

21.invariant: best tracks the minimum over all tried coins.

22.why: A cheaper coin combination was found.
22.invariant: best is the smallest coin count seen for this amount.

23.why: This amount is now solved once and for all.
23.invariant: The cell turns green and is reused if revisited.

24.happening: We return this amount's answer to the caller.
24.why: The caller adds it into its own count.
24.invariant: Every solved amount returns its cached minimum.

init.happening: Build the memo table and seed the base case.
init.invariant: Only memo[0] is known at first.

recurse.why: Each amount is solved from smaller amounts.

check.happening: Test a base case, a cache hit, or a coin fit.
check.why: These decide whether to recurse, reuse, or skip.

update.happening: Improve or cache a coin count.

loop.why: The best answer is the minimum across coins.

return.happening: Return a solved amount's minimum coins.
return.why: The value flows back up the recursion.
return.invariant: The final return is memo[amount] or -1.
